text:
maria: :rotating_light: Seeing apiserver watch lag + controller-manager leader flips in eu-west1. Grafana shows an etcd compaction job spiking wal/io and snapshot throughput around 02:00 UTC. Pod attach to GPU pools also delayed. Anyone else?
jon: ugh, compaction job ran at 02:00 — that's the periodic kv-compact-runner cron. I see EBS iops at 98% and queue depth skyrocket.
sam: confirmed. logs from etcd-0: 
```
sam: 2026-03-20T02:00:12Z etcdserver: processed snapshot, wal-sync-duration=0.67s iops=1300
sam: 2026-03-20T02:01:05Z etcdserver: snapshot write stalled, retrying
```
sam: also seeing apiserver apply queues growing, watch reconnects increasing.
cheng: controller-manager lost leader at 02:02 and we had 3 quick leader elections. That churn caused reconciliation spikes that hit GPU autoscaler and created attach backlog.
leah: prelim cost note: those failed attach retries + extra API calls are inflating request bill for the cluster (controller retries, kubelet backoff). Need to quantify after we stabilize.
dave: quick mitigation suggestions: 1) pause the kv-compact-runner cron for next run; 2) reduce compaction concurrency on the job from 4 -> 1; 3) increase etcd snapshot throttle (if supported) or run snapshot during low-traffic window; 4) temporarily increase controller-manager lease duration (extend --leader-elect-lease-duration) to reduce election churn.
maria: I'm going to pause the cron now and scale compaction job to 1. Doing patch: `kubectl -n infra scale job/kv-compact-runner --replicas=1`
ops-bot: deploybot: patch applied by maria: scale job/kv-compact-runner to 1 at 02:05 UTC
jon: good. Also we should bump EBS gp3 iops burst or switch the etcd PVs to a higher iops class for a couple hours while we run recovery. I can open a ticket with cloud to increase iops for /data-etcd (manual resize takes 5-10m).
sam: pushing a temporary RBAC patch to reduce watch fanout from some high-volume consumers: temporarily set `--watch-cache=2000`? (we should be cautious). Maybe instead block a couple noisy controllers from watching entire namespaces.
cheng: FYI GPU attach backlog clears faster once controller churn stops. After pause, attachments went from 600 pending -> 70 in ~12m.
leah: action list for post-incident: - quantify incremental cloud spend, - review compaction schedule and quorum snapshot size, - add a low-IO snapshot option, - add e2e test for compaction on a stressed disk. I'll create the ticket.
dave: operational runbook updates: add a safety gate to the compaction job: detect high disk utilization / apiserver watch lag and postpone. Also add circuit breaker to controller-manager leader election rate.
maria: note — we also saw NAT SNAT port count creeping higher in the same AZ; ssh proxy logs show ephemeral ports exhausted for a few minutes which coincided with failed kubelet -> apiserver connections. Might be contributing to reconnect slowness.
jon: ok open cloud support ticket for SNAT scaling and EBS iops bump. Tagging @cloud-systems.
sam: low-impact patch deployed to throttle snapshot concurrency: `--snapshot-concurrency=1` on compact job.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0319-49 by maria, priority P2, assigned eng-sre + cloud-systems.
cheng: monitoring notes: add alert for etcd wal_sync_duration > 0.5s sustained AND apiserver_watch_reconnects > 50 per minute; trigger runbook.
leah: assigning postmortem: leah (owner), sam (metrics), jon (cloud), maria (ops steps), cheng (k8s controllers). I'll draft timeline.
dave: temporary config we've set: compaction concurrency=1, controller lease-duration increased by 50% (applied to controller-manager deployment), cron paused. We'll revert after full review.
maria: followers: keep an eye on eu-west1 for 1 hour, if watchers and attach backlog stay low we can call this mitigated.
jon: noted. I'll follow up with cloud concerning iops & SNAT.
sam: good recovery signal: apiserver watch lag down to normal, etcd wal sync < 0.2s, controller-manager leader stable.
leah: thanks team. Postmortem template in #postmortems will be filled out, tag me when timeline is ready. :thumbsup:
